real_qa.q: What housing programs does Rocky View Foundation offer to seniors and low-income residents?
real_qa.r: Rocky View Foundation is a not-for-profit housing management body that delivers sustainable housing programs at non-market rates. The foundation operates senior lodges with supportive living services including meals, housekeeping and activities, manages four apartment buildings, and administers a rental assistance benefit program that allows individuals to access the private rental market while receiving benefits to help pay for rent.
real_qa.requete: Rocky View Foundation housing programs seniors

real_qa.q: How has the Rocky View Foundation rental assistance benefit program grown since taking it over in 2023?
real_qa.r: When Rocky View Foundation took over the rental assistance benefit program in 2023, there were about 60 people on the program with a couple hundred thousand in funding being delivered from Calgary. The foundation grew the program to now serve approximately 170 people with 1.5 million in annual funding, though there are currently 200 people on the wait list.
real_qa.requete: Rocky View Foundation rental assistance 2023 growth

real_qa.q: What is the capital stack funding model used by Rocky View Foundation to develop affordable housing?
real_qa.r: Rocky View Foundation uses a capital stack approach to acquire and develop more affordable housing by combining multiple funding sources. This includes donations and fundraising, land contributions from municipalities or donors, and stacked federal and provincial funds. Abrio Place, opened in Airdrie in 2023, exemplified this model by combining municipal capital, donor money, federal funds, and provincial funding to complete the project.
real_qa.requete: Rocky View Foundation capital stack affordable housing

real_qa.q: Which municipalities does Rocky View Foundation partner with to serve affordable housing communities in Alberta?
real_qa.r: Rocky View Foundation partners with six different municipalities: Airdrie, Cochrane, Crossfield, Ericana, Bicycle, and Rocky View County. The foundation describes each municipality as being very supportive of affordable housing initiatives.
real_qa.requete: Rocky View Foundation partner municipalities Alberta

real_qa.q: What real difference does affordable supportive living housing make for seniors transitioning from homelessness?
real_qa.r: Rocky View Foundation has seen seniors come from unfinished basements and living in vehicles who were able to find affordable housing with the foundation. Accessing supportive living at rates seniors can afford unlocks tangible outcomes including increased physical and mental health outcomes, community connection, and improved social outcomes that would not be accessible at market rates.
real_qa.requete: affordable housing seniors health outcomes outcomes homelessness

guest.bio_context: Chris Rowe is British Columbia born and raised who spent two years in Dallas, Texas before moving to Alberta. He brings a background in real estate, finance, and HR with a hospitality company managing commercial assets. Prior to joining Rocky View Foundation, he spent two years working with an indigenous community on social housing initiatives, where he secured two large projects through COVID-era housing program grants.
